category.title: 1. Category
category.body: The shelf a product sits on, e.g. “VPN” or “API services”. It only organises and displays.

product.title: 2. Product
product.body: What the customer knows, e.g. “VPN Pro”. It sets how it is delivered and which capabilities a purchase unlocks.

variant.title: 3. Variant
variant.body: What is actually sold: duration, quotas (traffic, devices) and visibility. A product with no variant cannot be bought.

price.title: 4. Price
price.body: Each variant keeps a price history. A new price never erases the old one; you can schedule it for a later day.

translations.title: 5. Translations
translations.body: Write the name in one language only. Tick “Translate into every language” to get machine drafts for the others; they are shown to users only after you publish them under “Translations”.

budget.tradeOff: This is the panel owner's limit on how often we may ask. Lower is gentler on their server and less likely to get our address banned, but a pass waits for its slots, so usage arrives later and ceilings are enforced later. Higher is fresher, and only safe if the owner agreed to it.

matrix.title: Acceptance questionnaire
matrix.stale: These answers are under an older questionnaire. The next connection test answers it again.
matrix.noMeteredSale: Accepted, but no metered sale: it cannot

per_client_usage.question: Does it report a usage figure for one named client, rather than only a server total?
per_client_usage.unmet: Refused: a server total cannot be split between the users on it, so there is nothing to bill.

bulk_usage_in_one_call.question: Can the usage of every client on the panel be read in a bounded number of requests: one, or one per page of at least 100 clients?
bulk_usage_in_one_call.unmet: Refused: a panel read client by client makes 5000 clients 5000 requests a pass on someone else's server.

usage_for_named_subset.question: Does one call return the usage of a named subset of clients?
usage_for_named_subset.unmet: Each pass re-reads the whole panel, so how often it runs is bounded by the cost of that call.

usage_reset_supported.question: Can a client's counter be zeroed on request?
usage_reset_supported.unmet: Nothing is lost: we only ever read a counter. A reset is something we detect, never something we cause.

counter_survives_client_update.question: Does a client's counter keep its value when the client is updated — a ceiling written, a label changed?
counter_survives_client_update.unmet: Every ceiling write looks like a reset, so the counter is re-read in the same pass as the write.

gigawords_reported.question: Does the NAS send the gigaword counters beside the 32-bit octet counters?
gigawords_reported.unmet: A session past 4 GB is held rather than billed, and never estimated.

per_client_data_limit.question: Can a byte ceiling be written for one client, and does the panel enforce it itself?
per_client_data_limit.unmet: No metered sale: the ceiling is the only limit that still works while our service is down.

data_limit_counts_the_same_bytes_as_usag.question: Does the enforced ceiling count the same bytes the usage figure reports — both directions, same units?
data_limit_counts_the_same_bytes_as_usag.unmet: No metered sale: a block bought against one number would be spent against another, and the gap is free traffic.

per_client_rate_limit.question: Can a bandwidth rate be written for one client?
per_client_rate_limit.unmet: A custom rate is recorded but not enforced on the panel; our own limiting stays.

per_client_ip_limit.question: Can a limit on the addresses one client connects from at once be written for that client?
per_client_ip_limit.unmet: A device limit is recorded but not enforced on this panel; the admin is told which panels ignore it.

enable_disable_client.question: Can one client be disabled and re-enabled without deleting it?
enable_disable_client.unmet: Refused: suspending would have to delete the client, and a top-up could not restore it.

client_lifecycle.question: Can a client be created, updated and deleted through the API?
client_lifecycle.unmet: Refused: nothing could be provisioned or removed.

stable_remote_id.question: Does a client carry an id that survives being renamed?
stable_remote_id.unmet: A renamed client reads as missing until the next matching key is tried.

client_label_storable.question: Can we store our own tag on the client — a note, label or remark field?
client_label_storable.unmet: A client rebuilt on the panel reads as an orphan rather than as ours.

native_subscription_link.question: Does the panel serve a subscription URL for a client?
native_subscription_link.unmet: We build the link ourselves, so a change reaches the user only when the link is fetched again.

server_side_expiry.question: Does the panel enforce an expiry date on a client by itself?
server_side_expiry.unmet: Expiry is ours alone: a service that ends while our loop is down keeps working until the loop returns.

internal_credit_disablable.question: Can the panel's own billing or credit be switched off, leaving us the only writer of the quota?
internal_credit_disablable.unmet: The panel cuts users off on its own schedule, so it is used for metering only.

drift.title: Drift report
drift.hint: What the collector found changed on a panel all at once. An event that halts collection waits for a person: acknowledging it resumes collection on the next pass.
drift.acknowledgeHint: Only once you know why it happened — a restore, a migration. Collection resumes on the next pass.
drift.done: Acknowledged. Collection resumes on the next pass.

drift.foreignHint: Not read and sent no change while this is open. Put the panel's address right first; acknowledged as it is, it is raised again on the next pass.

holds.queued: Queued for the meter. The hold stays waiting until it is billed.
holds.writeOffHint: These bytes are never charged. Say why — the note is kept with your name.

resubmit.title: Re-submit this panel's login
resubmit.hint: The new login replaces the stored one in the vault; the old one is not shown or kept here. A panel still waiting for its test is tested again on the next pass.

outcome.retest: Saved. The panel is tested again on the next pass.
outcome.coolingOff: Saved. The panel was rate-limiting us, so its next test waits out the cool-off.
outcome.rotated: Saved. Collection uses the new login from its next pass.

radiusSecret.title: Re-submit this panel's RADIUS secret
radiusSecret.hint: The NAS signs every accounting packet with this secret. The new one replaces the stored one; packets are accepted under it within a minute. The panel is not tested again.
radiusSecret.saved: Saved. Accounting from this NAS is checked against the new secret within a minute.

groups.title: Panel groups
groups.hint: Where a VPN product's users get their configs. A variant names a group, and each Grant sold on it gets configs on every member that is accepted and healthy — on the inbounds each panel sells (Panels → Inbounds). Changes reach what is placed next, within a minute.
groups.empty: No groups yet. A VPN variant cannot be sold until it names one.
groups.editHint: Changes reach configs placed from now on; configs already placed stay where they are. Which inbounds, and so which protocols, is set on each panel.

field.name: Name
field.minHealthyPanelsHint: A Grant turns active once this many of its configs are live.
field.ttlHint: How often users' apps re-read their subscription. Draining a member waits twice this, so every app has moved first.

invalid.name: A name of 1 to 100 characters.
invalid.ttlMinutes: A whole number of minutes, from 1 to 10080 (a week).

health.short: Only {{placeable}} member(s) take new configs, and {{min}} are needed: a Grant sold now waits until more are accepted and healthy.

members.title: Members
members.empty: No panels yet. Nothing sold on this group can be delivered until it has one.
members.waiting: Takes nothing new until its panel is accepted and healthy

add.label: Add a registered panel
add.none: Every registered panel that is not refused is already in this group.
add.hint: It takes new configs once its panel is accepted and healthy; Grants already sold on this group are placed on it within a minute.

drain.confirmHint: It takes no new configs. Each user is given another member's line first; this panel's configs go no sooner than {{wait}} after that, and the member leaves the group on its own. No user is cut off.
drain.started: Draining. Its configs go no sooner than {{wait}} from now — later for a Grant whose replacement is not served yet.
drain.since: Draining since {{since}} · configs go no sooner than {{at}}

settings.takesNobody: not on sale on the panel, or disabled there — takes nobody
settings.sellsNobody: Nothing this group sells here is on sale and enabled: it places nobody on this panel.

inbounds.title: Inbounds sold on this panel
inbounds.hint: Tick the inbounds a buyer is placed on. With nothing ticked, nobody is placed on this panel. A change reaches the next buyer; configs already placed stay where they are.

placement.label: How a buyer is placed
placement.allHint: Each buyer gets a config on every ticked inbound, one link each. Their traffic is shared across them.
placement.spread: On one ticked inbound, the emptiest
placement.spreadHint: Each buyer gets one config, on the ticked inbound with the fewest users that is under its cap.

inbounds.panelMaxHint: Empty = no cap. At the cap, no new buyer is placed here; buyers already here keep their configs.
inbounds.notRead: Not read yet — within a minute of the panel's next pass
inbounds.refreshed: Asked. The inbounds are read again on the panel's next pass, within a minute.
inbounds.unknownProtocol: A protocol we do not sell
inbounds.nothingPicked: Nothing is ticked: no buyer is placed on this panel.
inbounds.saved: Saved. The next buyer is placed this way.

invalid.cap: A whole number from 1, or empty for no cap.

inbounds.poolHint: An inbound a group has taken is sold only by that group; the rest are the pool every other group on this panel shares.

edit.loginHint: Leave blank to keep the stored login. A new one replaces it in the vault and is never shown again.
edit.pushAddresses: A push panel reports to us, so it has no API or link address — only the NAS IP the allowlist trusts.
edit.ipHint: The NAS's address. The allowlist reads a change within a minute.
edit.addressWarning: You changed an address. The panel goes back to its connection test, and collection pauses until the new address passes — usually within a minute.
edit.savedRetest: Saved. The new address is tested on the next pass; collection resumes once it passes.
edit.invalidBudget: Enter a whole number from 1 to 6000.

remove.title: Delete {{panel}}?
remove.hint: If this panel never had users, it is deleted for good. If it had, it is archived instead: hidden from this list, no longer tested or collected, and its usage and history kept. You can restore an archived panel later.
remove.blockedGroups: It is still a member of {{groups}}. Remove it from each group first — or drain it, if users still have configs on it.
remove.archived: It had history, so it was archived: hidden from the list, no longer collected, its records kept.

groupsRemove.title: Delete the group {{group}}?
groupsRemove.hint: The group is deleted for good.
groupsRemove.blockedMembers: It still has {{n}} member(s). Remove or drain them first.
groupsRemove.blockedVariants: {{n}} variant(s) sell on it. In the catalog, move them to another group first.

refusalsNamed.panel_already_registered: This API address is already registered as “{{panel}}”. Edit or restore that panel instead of registering it again.
refusalsNamed.inbound_assigned_elsewhere: Inbound #{{inbound}} is already sold only by group “{{group}}”. Take it off that group's member first.
refusalsNamed.inbound_has_configs: Buyers of another group still have {{configs}} configs on inbound #{{inbound}}. Drain that group's member on this panel first, so they are moved.

guide.title: Start selling VPN in 4 steps
guide.intro: Someone can buy VPN once these four steps are done, in order. Each step ticks itself when it is done.
guide.allDone: All four steps are done and sales are running. From now on, just check the tabs that show a red number.

register.title: Register a panel
register.body: Tell us about the server your VPN panel (3x-ui, Marzban…) runs on: its address and an admin account.

accepted.title: Pass the connection test
accepted.body: After you register, we connect to the panel and test it — usually under a minute. Nothing to do unless it is refused.

group.title: Create a group and add the panel
group.body: A group is a set of panels that sell one product together. Create one and add an accepted panel to it.

product.title: Link a product to the group
product.body: In the catalog, pick this group for a VPN product. From then on every purchase creates configs on the group's panels.

panel.body: The VPN management software on your server (3x-ui, Marzban or a MikroTik router). We create buyers' configs and read their usage through it.

test.body: After you register, we connect to the panel and check we can create users and read usage. Nothing is sold on it until it passes.

inbound.body: An entry point on the panel with a set protocol and port, e.g. vless on port 443. Each buyer's config is created on one or more inbounds.

group.body: Several panels that sell one product together. Each purchase gets a config on every healthy panel in the group, so if one fails the others keep working.

shared.body: By default every group on a panel sells on that panel's ticked inbounds (shared). Give a group dedicated inbounds and those belong to that group alone.

drain.body: Taking a panel out of a group gently: it gets no new configs, its users move to the group's other panels without being cut off, and then it leaves the group.

tabs.panelsHint: The servers you registered. Open a panel's "Settings" to see and change its address, the inbounds it sells and its login.
tabs.reportsHint: Changes seen on panels and usage held back for review. Usually empty; if a number shows, take a look.

ready.label: Ready to sell
ready.hint: The panel is accepted and healthy; new configs are created on it.

limited.label: Ready, with limits
limited.hint: Accepted, but it did not answer yes to every test question; metered sales may be off on it. Details: Settings → Test result.

testing.label: Being tested
testing.hint: Give it under a minute; the result shows up here by itself.

refused.label: Refused
refused.hint: This panel failed the connection test and nothing is sold on it. Why is under Settings → Test result.

problem.label: Needs attention
problem.hint: Accepted, but something is stopping it right now:

panelSheet.title: {{panel}} settings
panelSheet.salesIntro: Choose which of this panel's inbounds buyers are created on. This applies to every group the panel is in, unless you set a group apart (Groups → Selling settings).
panelSheet.pushNoSales: This is a push (RADIUS) panel: we never connect to it, so it has no inbounds to choose.
panelSheet.loginHint: If you changed the panel's password, give the new login here.

member.title: Selling "{{group}}" on {{panel}}
member.intro: By default this group sells on this panel exactly as the panel's own settings say. Pick "own" only where this group should differ here. A change applies from the next buyer; existing configs are untouched.
member.placement: How many inbounds does a config go on?
member.cap: Most users of this group on this panel
member.capHint: This group's cap cannot go above the panel's own.
member.poolHint: The inbounds ticked for sale in the panel's settings, except those another group has taken as dedicated.
member.ownInboundsHint: The inbounds you tick belong to this group alone; other groups stop selling on them.
member.saved: Saved. This group's next buyer is created with these settings.

leave.title: Take this panel out of the group
leave.hint: "Remove" works only while no user has a config on this panel. If some do, "Drain" moves them to the group's other panels without cutting them off.

invalid.cap: Write a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000, or pick "Same as the panel".
invalid.pickOne: Tick at least one inbound, or pick "The panel's shared inbounds".

groupCard.noProduct: No product is sold on this group yet. To start selling, pick this group for a VPN product in the catalog.
